annotations.title: Would refitting have helped? (out of sample)

description:
Whether re-optimising an allocation would have helped: refit on the years
        before each date, hold it on prices it had not seen, repeat, and
        compare that record with the portfolio actually held and with equal
        weight. Says whether refitting bought anything measurable. Returns the
        record, never an allocation to hold.

base.description: Currency every figure is expressed in (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD…). Default USD.
base.title: Base

holdings.description: Optional: the portfolio actually held, {ticker: weight}, measured on the same span for comparison.
holdings.title: Holdings

objective.description: What each refit maximises or minimises: max_sharpe, min_variance, min_drawdown, min_cvar or max_quadratic_utility.
objective.title: Objective

step_months.description: Months each fitted mix is held.
step_months.title: Step Months

train_years.description: Years of history each refit sees.
train_years.title: Train Years

name: walk_forward

outputSchema.description: An allocation method tested out of sample; no allocation is returned.

_fence.description: What these figures are and are not: descriptive, no forecast, no advice. Repeat its sense when presenting the result.

data.description: Where the prices came from and what was missing or repaired.

as_of.description: Last date of price history used.

missing.description: Tickers with no usable history (left out).

standins.description: Holdings measured through a stand-in with longer history: ticker, proxy, index, from, until, evidence.

fitted_window.description: First and last date of shared history.

out_of_sample.description: start, end, n_refits, train_years, step_months, mean_turnover, verdict (one sentence on the record), limitations, tracks (per track: label, cagr, vol, sharpe, max_drawdown, nav), refits (date, turnover); or `unavailable` with the reason.

title: Would refitting have helped? (out of sample)
